title: will be doing and will have done
subtitle: I will be doing / I will have done
summary: Use will be doing for an action in progress at a future time, and will have done for an action that will be complete before a future time.

lesson.heading: Study this situation
lesson.text: Imagine some people standing in a queue to get into the cinema. Half an hour from now, the cinema **will be** full. Everyone **will be watching** the film. Three hours from now, the cinema will be empty. The film **will have finished**. Everyone **will have gone** home.

examples.text: Half an hour from now: everyone **will be watching** the film.
Three hours from now: the film **will have finished**. Everyone **will have gone** home.

lesson.heading: I will be doing = in the middle of doing it
lesson.text: **I will be doing something** (future continuous) = I will be in the middle of doing it at that time. Compare will be (do)ing and will (do).

examples.text: This time next week I'll be on holiday. **I'll be lying** on the beach or swimming in the sea.
You have no chance of getting the job. **You'll be wasting** your time if you apply.
Don't phone between 7 and 8. **We'll be eating.**
Let's wait for Liz to arrive and then **we'll eat**.

lesson.heading: Tina in her office: past, present, future
rows: Tina was in her office. She **was working**.
She is in her office. She **is working**.
She will be in her office. She **will be working**.

lesson.heading: will be -ing for complete future actions
lesson.text: We also use **will be -ing** to talk about complete actions in the future, often for planned events. Used in this way, will be (doing) is similar to will (do) and going to (do).

examples.text: The government **will be making** a statement about the crisis later today.
Later in the programme, **I'll be talking** to the Minister of Education.
The team's star player is injured and **won't be playing** in the game on Saturday.

lesson.heading: I will have done = complete before a future time
lesson.text: **I will have done something** (future perfect) = it will be complete before a time in the future.

examples.text: Sally always leaves for work at 8.30 in the morning. She won't be at home at 9 o'clock - **she'll have gone** to work.
We're late. The film **will already have started** by the time we get to the cinema.

lesson.heading: Ted and Amy: three perfect tenses
rows: Ted and Amy **have been** married for 24 years.
Next year they **will have been** married for 25 years.
When their son was born, they **had been** married for three years.

lesson.text: Picture the future moment. Still going on at that moment? will be doing. Already over by that moment? will have done.

exercises.prompt: Half an hour from now the cinema will be full. Everyone ___ the film.
exercises.explanation: At that future moment the film will be in progress: will be watching.

exercises.statement: Andy leaves home at 8 o'clock every day. Tomorrow at 8.15 he'll be leaving the house.
exercises.explanation: At 8.15 he'll have left the house. Leaving is complete before 8.15, so the future perfect.

exercises.prompt: Tomorrow afternoon we're going to play tennis from 3 o'clock until 4.30. So at 4 o'clock, ___ tennis.
exercises.explanation: At 4 o'clock the game will be in progress: we'll be playing.

exercises.prompt: At the future time mentioned, is the action in progress or already complete?

items.text: Everyone will be watching the film.
Don't phone between 7 and 8. We'll be eating.
She won't be at home at 9 - she'll have gone to work.
The film will already have started by the time we get there.
This time next week I'll be lying on the beach.

exercises.prompt: Emily is not well, so she ___ volleyball tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: A planned future event she will not take part in: she won't be playing.

exercises.statement: Andy goes home from work at exactly 4.30 every day. Tomorrow at 4.45 he'll have left work.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Leaving work is complete before 4.45, so will have left is right.

exercises.prompt: Sarah will meet you at the station. ___ for you when you arrive.
exercises.explanation: The waiting will be in progress when you arrive: She'll be waiting.

exercises.prompt: Ted and Amy have been married for 24 years. Say what will be true next year.
exercises.answer: Next year they will have been married for 25 years.
exercises.explanation: Future perfect: will have + past participle (been).

exercises.prompt: Lisa is travelling in Europe and so far she has travelled about 1,000 miles. By the end of the trip, ___ more than 3,000 miles.
exercises.explanation: Complete by a future point (the end of the trip): she'll have travelled.

exercises.prompt: Sally always leaves for work at 8.30 in the morning. She won't be at home at 9 o'clock - ___ to work.
exercises.explanation: By 9 o'clock her leaving is complete: she'll have gone.

exercises.prompt: Ben is on holiday and is spending his money very quickly. If he continues like this, ___ all his money before the end of his holiday.
exercises.explanation: Complete before a future time (the end of his holiday): he'll have spent.

exercises.statement: Andy works until exactly 4.30 every day. Tomorrow at 4 o'clock he'll have finished work.
exercises.explanation: At 4 o'clock he'll be working - he won't have finished work until 4.30.
